engine.summary:
Engine fix pass on top of the round 6 colour cure. Started 04:03, last source change 05:10, smoke test on the final build 05:12, stopped 05:17 (74 minutes). Final page: dist/r7-engine.html (base7a plus my three files). Notes with everything per defect: .../scratch-2026-11-17-a06af1/notes/r7-engine.md. Scripts, logs, pictures: .../scratch-2026-11-17-a06af1/out/r7/engine/.

Majors: solids-2 fixed (a thin trap keeps its pieces), solids-1 was already cured by round 6 (shown with the tester's steps), mesh-1 fixed on my side (model colours now read from the surface with the picture's number of steps; a regression of round 6 in the Kleinian model found and cured too), kleinian-1 NOT fixed: the cause is found and proved with four pictures, it is not the third map and not the march, and the page now says when it happens. Minors: flat-2, flat-3, flat-5, solids-3, solids-6, walk-2 done; solids-4 has notes only; flat-4 is not the iteration limit (measured) and got a true sentence; solids-5, words-4, words-5 not fixed.

Must-not-change pictures: 28 of 30 identical to dist/v7a.html (largest channel difference 0); the other two are an inside coloured by the trap, changed on purpose by flat-5. Of the 55 tester scenes 46 are identical to v7a and the 9 that differ are the ones a defect asked to change. Smoke test tools/smoke-v6.json passes on the final build: 42 steps, exit 0, no console errors.

Compile time kept: opening Mandelbrot program 1.85 to 2.03 s (limit 2.6), Kleinian 0.81 to 0.91 s (limit 1.1), the same as v7a. This needed one structural step: the code for 3D model samples lives in a program of its own (RAW_FIT), because inside the picture's program it cost half a second (measured 2.53 to 2.57 s).

Honest gaps: drawing time is within a quarter of base4 only by the least visit (M 418 against 341 ms); most Mandelbrot visits of v7a AND of my page read about twice base4 on the shared GPU, so that target is not shown for v7a or for this round. The tester scenes were drawn on the 04:49 build, not again on the final one, which differs only inside #if RAW_FIT (reasoned to be identical; the 30 fixed pictures were drawn again on the 05:03 build, the smoke test on the 05:10 build).

Same change in the colour module's touch record and its 'too fine to colour' test. Thickness 0.05 and more: nothing changes.

fixed.what: Samples for the 3D model now carry the picture's colours. A sample of an equation within 1.5 spacings inside to 3.2 outside (by estimate) finds the surface along its own slope (two readings) and reads the trap colour there with the picture's own number of orbit steps (uPx carries the picture's height for these draws). A Kleinian sample makes one more query in which the search lands on the pearl beside it (round 6 had made the picture do that but not the model, which broke a match that v6 had). A sample deep inside, or inside the solid in the slices around the cut plane, gets the cut face's colour (hatching evened out, or the inside colouring when the cut face is painted). fixed.what: While the graphics context is lost the status line reads 'The graphics of this page were interrupted. The picture comes back by itself.' (LOST_WORDS, said in the webglcontextlost listener).
fixed.evidence: out/r7/engine/repro-final.log step 35: before 'Done: 12 passes at 862 x 701'; 0.4 s after the loss and again after clicking Julia: the new sentence; after restoreContext: 'Done: 12 passes ...'. No console errors. idle() is unchanged (still true while lost).

not_fixed.why: The cut pieces are a property of how the Kleinian trap solid is defined, not of the march, and the cure is a new definition that I could not build and check in the time. A note now warns in plain words when it will happen.
not_fixed.learned: Measured with four pictures (out/r7/engine/x-sheet-1.png, first row; before: before-kleinian.png): entry 3 with the third map switched ON is still sliced; entry 0 with it switched OFF is still whole; entry 0 with the trap centre at x = 0.6 is sliced. So the third map has nothing to do with it: entries 3 and 24 have a real part of mu = 1. Reasoned cause: the search carries a point into one copy of the pattern (slide by 2, half turn about mu/2) and tests the trap after each map; a piece that reaches across the edge of a copy is tested there against another part of the trap, so it ends at the edge (the flat faces). With both leans of mu at 0 and the trap centred on x = 0, z = 0 the two sides of every edge are mirror images, so the piece carries on as its reflection: that is the only reason entries 0 and 21 look whole. Shortening the step cannot help. A cure: test the trap only at the two points the search comes to rest on (the same for a whole orbit), with their neighbours across each edge, instead of at every step; that changes every Kleinian trap solid and the meaning of 'steps skipped' there. Also seen: entry 0 with trap centre y = 0.5 gives a black stage (camera inside a piece). Done instead: note under the choice, shown by colKleinCuts (on entry 3 yes, on entry 0 no: repro-final.log step 20).

not_fixed.why: Needs a different rule for which layers are drawn, which changes every trap solid. Not started.
not_fixed.learned: The holes are layers eaten in patches by the thin layer rule: it removes a layer where its wall is under two pixels, which at the opening view is a stretch of 5 to 7.5, and a bubble made by step 3 or later straddles that (reasoned from the code and the pictures before-solids-b.png). Removing a layer as a whole needs a rule by step number or by the size of the piece instead of wall thickness. Pictures unchanged: identical to v7a.

not_fixed.why: The look-alike objects themselves are unchanged; only notes were added.
not_fixed.learned: Julia c = -1: every inside orbit ends on the trap centre, so the note says to move the centre (tested: Point, centre x 0.5, thickness 0.2 gives chains of beads, x-sheet-1.png). Kleinian: Point, Line and Ray give the same lace because the lace is the deep fine layers, which the Kleinian solid has no rule to thin out; such a rule would also take the lace off the pictures the tester liked. The Kleinian note says the three look alike and names the four shapes that do not.

not_fixed.why: It is not the iteration limit, so the suggested hint would have been false, and the soft shapes are what an outline drawn from the distance estimate gives there.
not_fixed.learned: Measured: at height 0.003 the picture at 2000 iterations (Extreme ranges on) is the same as at 300 (out/r7/engine/flat4-300-vs-2000.png). My first try (1500 set through the state) was no test, because the dial holds the count at 400 without Extreme ranges. Reasoned: deep in a spiral the set is a web of threads, each drawn about a pixel wide by the estimate, and they run together. The help of 'Outline width, pixels' now says that, and that more iterations do not change it.

Measured on v7a and on my page (identical pictures): in the tester's side view at distance 4.6 the rough estimate draws 2993 pixels that the exact one leaves as background (3.3 % of the solid; the tester had 5.5 % on v6) and misses 3025 that the exact one draws. In my pictures the dark striped band under the lower edge is in the EXACT picture, not the rough one (out/r7/engine/before-words4-crop.png, rough above, exact below), which is the reverse of the report. Whether round 6 moved it was not established.

not_fixed.why: The cause is not the one named, and the likely cure touches the shadow gauge of the rough estimate, which needs its own checks.
not_fixed.learned: Reproduced (out/r7/engine/ref/d-words-5-ultra-i40.png). Measured: it is not rays running out of steps, with 300 steps in place of 90 the wedge is the same (x-sheet-1.png, last row). Ultra fast has no shadows, so it is not a shadow. Reasoned, not tried: the four slope samples of the rough estimate, whose size is wrong by a factor that changes from place to place at 40 iterations, give wrong surface directions. A cure would take the slope samples with the exact estimate when the march is rough and measure the gauge for shadows separately.

names_added: TRAP_REF (const, GL_HEAD in 30-shaders.js): 0.05, a trap thinner than this fades as one of this thickness would, in proportion
RAW_FIT (macro 0 or 1, written by glNeeds): 1 in the program volume samples are drawn with; GL_TAIL defines it as 1 when it is not defined
glNeeds(needs, klein): writes a fourth line, #define RAW_FIT, from needs.raw
glNeedsKey(needs): adds 'r' for needs.raw; keys of the model's programs end in r (for example klein|r, ...|sr); every other program key is unchanged

RAW_OUT, RAW_IN, RAW_CUT, RAW_ABOVE, RAW_HATCH (consts, GL_TAIL): 3.2, 1.5, 1.01, 3.01, 0.12: which samples read their colour from the surface (by estimate, in sample spacings), which slices make the cut face (1.01 below the cut plane to 3.01 above), share of ink in the model's cut face
rawCut, rawFace (locals of main()): this volume sample is coloured as the cut face; this slice is one the cut face is made between

crawl, ts, tIn, dOut in the flat branch of main(): reused for a volume sample: query count (0 the sample, 1 and 2 the readings, 3 the colour), place and value of the reading before, the distance the sample itself read
uPx for a volume sample (uniform, set in sampleSlice): the height of the snapshot's picture in page pixels (was 1)
uPalInO (uniform, GL_COLOUR): added to the palette shift for the inside; half a turn while the inside is coloured by the trap in the outside's palette, else 0
snap.wantRaw, snap.PR, snap.genR (40-render.js): a snapshot's program for volume samples, started when a model first asks for it
snapProg(snap, raw), snapReady(snap, raw): second argument selects the program for volume samples; without it they behave as before (45-export.js needs no change)
takeSnapshot / releaseSnapshot: make and unpin the second program entry
LOST_WORDS (40-render.js): the status line while the graphics context is lost
colTrapThin(c) (25-colour.js): the trap is a point, a line or a ray
colKleinCuts(c) (25-colour.js): a Kleinian trap solid would show cut pieces (mu has a real or j part, or the trap centre is off x = 0, z = 0)
colViewSync (25-colour.js): its signature also holds whether mu leans, so the Kleinian note comes and goes with the dials
setColourUniforms: uCutFace and uInMode are now set for volume samples too (were forced to 0 there); sets uPalInO
pixelColour kind COL_CUT (GL_COLOUR): 'how deep inside' reads d as handed in; also used for volume samples inside the solid
colPick (GL_COLOUR): inside colouring 4 in the Kleinian program shows the depth
main() cut face query PH_CUT: qn = 3 when uInMode is 3 (was always 0)

Texts in COLOUR_CONTROLS: note under 'In the 3D view the trap' rewritten; three new notes there (thin shapes, thin shapes in the Kleinian view, cut pieces in the Kleinian view); note for the inside coloured by the trap extended; new note for 'How quickly the orbit settles' in the Kleinian view; help of 'Outline width, pixels' extended. No control id, state key or option value changed
needs_from_others: src/js/46-mesh.js, meshPoint(): the colour weight is 'w = din <= 0 ? 1 : s' (outside end only when the inside end is in the solid). Both ends now hold the colour of the surface nearest to them whenever they read between 1.5 spacings inside and 3.2 outside, so blend by the point's place on the edge for every surface edge (w = s).

src/js/46-mesh.js, meshPoint(), cut face: for a point whose outside end is outside only because of the cut plane or the grid wall, take the colour from an end whose own distance is at or below zero (it holds the cut face's colour). Where both ends read above zero the point lies in the band by which the model is fatter than the solid: that is the coloured rim of the cut face today (out/r7/engine/mesh/r7-engine/pics/cmp-cut-128.png). It goes when offset 0 means 'where the picture has it' (mesh-4), or give the whole cut face the colour of the nearest end inside the solid.

src/js/46-mesh.js, panel text: the first model of a formula now waits about 3 s while the model's own program is prepared (measured 3.8 s for the first 128 cell job, 0.5 to 1.6 s after). A line such as 'Preparing the model' for that time would explain the wait.

src/body.html, closing text, sentence 'This works in Mandelbrot, Julia and Kleinian pictures, and the solid keeps its colours at every quality setting.': not true for every Kleinian group. Suggested: 'This works in Mandelbrot and Julia pictures and in Kleinian pictures whose group does not lean (the real part and the j part of mu at 0). In a leaning group some pieces come out cut open, and the page says so beside the choice. The solid keeps its colours at every quality setting.'

src/body.html, closing text, after 'The inside can stay Plain, or be coloured by Orbit trap, Where the orbit ends up, How deep inside, or How quickly the orbit settles ...': add 'In the Kleinian view the last of these shows the depth, because that search has nothing that settles. Coloured by the orbit trap in the outside's own palette, the inside starts half-way round the palette, so that the set does not look like a hole.'

src/body.html, closing text, sentence 'Such rays now get past the solid, and a ray that runs out of steps away from the surface shows the background.': still not quite true with the roughest estimate (words-4, words-5 are open). Suggested addition: 'With the Rough distance estimate the outline can still differ a little from the exact one, and at Ultra fast with many iterations a bead can show a dark patch. Balanced has neither.'

src/body.html, closing text, 'Save a 3D model turns the solid into a mesh ...': could add 'Its colours are read from the surface the same way the picture's are, and a solid that is cut open gets the plain colour of the cut face there.' (true once the mesh change above is in).

src/body.html: any sentence telling the reader to lower the iterations to thin out a trap solid no longer matches the page's own note (it now names trap thickness, steps skipped, trap radius and centre).

Person joining the files: take 25-colour.js, 30-shaders.js and 40-render.js together (25 needs TRAP_REF from 30; 40 writes needs.raw; 30 expects uPx to mean the picture's height for volume samples). tools/smoke-v6.json passes unchanged. A smoke step that times a model job should allow about 4 s more for the first model of a page.
